column3: The Hebrew says Moses went and spoke these words; BSB says “When Moses had finished speaking these words.”
The Hebrew says “go out and come in” and explicitly calls the river “this Jordan”; BSB has “come and go” and “the Jordan.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses singular collective “the Amorite”; BSB uses plural “the Amorites.”
The Hebrew explicitly says “according to the whole commandment”; BSB expresses this as “exactly as I have commanded you.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “before the eyes of all Israel”; BSB says “in the presence of all Israel.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names a year of “release” without an explicit noun “debt”; BSB specifies “remission of debt.”
The Hebrew explicitly names the LORD’s “face” and Israel’s “ears”; BSB says to come “before the LORD” and read “in the hearing” of Israel.
The Hebrew uses singular “your foreigner”; BSB has plural “the foreigners.”
The Hebrew does not explicitly supply an object after “have not known”; BSB supplies “the law.”
The Hebrew says “your days have drawn near to die”; BSB expresses this as “the time of your death is near.”
The Hebrew repeats “the pillar of cloud” as what stood at the entrance; BSB says “the cloud” the second time.
The Hebrew says to lie with the fathers and uses the image of cutting the covenant; BSB has “rest with your fathers” and “made” the covenant.
The Hebrew alternates singular and plural references to the people, including singular “my God” and “me” in their question; BSB consistently uses plural pronouns, including “our God” and “us.”
The Hebrew refers to the people’s action with singular verbs; BSB uses plural “they.”
The Hebrew says to put the song “in their mouth” and repeats “this song” and “the sons of Israel”; BSB has “have them recite it” and uses pronouns for the repeated nouns.
The Hebrew uses the image of becoming fat; BSB says “prosper.” The Hebrew does not explicitly include “to give” in the oath clause, which BSB supplies.
The Hebrew explicitly includes “today” with their inclination and activity, and its final oath clause does not explicitly include “to give them”; BSB omits “today” and supplies “to give them.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew begins with an unnamed “he commissioned”; BSB explicitly names the LORD.
The Hebrew says “until their completion”; BSB says “from beginning to end.”
The Hebrew explicitly names Moses again; BSB uses “he.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names “your rebellion” and “your hard neck”; BSB expresses these as “how rebellious and stiff-necked you are.”
The Hebrew explicitly says to speak “in their ears”; BSB says “in their hearing.”
The Hebrew says “evil in the eyes of the LORD”; BSB uses “evil in the sight of the LORD.”
The Hebrew says Moses spoke “in the ears” of the assembly “until their completion”; BSB has “recited aloud” and “from beginning to end.”
